subject: Proposition 2.5 Ballot Questions
overview: City Councilor Matt Leming reviewed three measures approved by the City Council for the November ballot, including two Proposition 2.5 overrides and a debt exclusion. He discussed the city's financial condition, the constraints of state tax law, and why he views the measures as essential.

items.title: Three November Ballot Measures
items.summary: Councilor Leming outlined three approved November ballot questions: a $3.5 million override for school level-funding and Department of Public Works staffing, a $4 million override for school investments and salaries, and a debt exclusion to construct a new fire headquarters.

items.title: Proposition 2.5 and Financial Context
items.summary: Leming explained how the statutory 2.5 percent tax levy cap and decades of inflation have strained municipal finances, leaving the city reliant on one-time reserves to sustain school operations.

items.title: Addressing Alternatives and the Operating Budget
items.summary: Leming addressed public questions regarding commercial development, spending cuts, and the city's $218 million budget, stating that long-term zoning changes will take years to yield revenue and that municipal spending has already been reduced to minimal levels.
